result.topic_en: Gauss defines (k/p) as the number of multiples k, 2k, ..., ½(p−1)k whose least positive residues mod p fall below ½p, and expresses it through sums of greatest-integer functions [x], with auxiliary identities for sums of [nx].
result.transcription:
164 [?] Litt. Q. [?]

Designemus per $\left(\frac{k}{p}\right)$ multitudinem productorum ex his $k, 2k, 3k \ldots \frac{1}{2}(p-1)k$, quorum residua minima positiva secundum modulum $p$ cadunt infra $\frac{1}{2}p$; porro per $[x]$ numerum integrum quantitate $x$ proxime minorem. Habebis

1) $\left(\frac{k}{p}\right) = \left[\frac{2k}{p}\right] + \left[\frac{4k}{p}\right] + \left[\frac{6k}{p}\right] \ldots + \left[\frac{(p-1)k}{p}\right]$
$-2\left[\frac{k}{p}\right] - 2\left[\frac{2k}{p}\right] - 2\left[\frac{3k}{p}\right] \ldots - 2\left[\frac{\frac{1}{2}(p-1)k}{p}\right]$

2) $[x] + [-x] = -1$
3) $\left(\frac{k}{p}\right) + \left(\frac{-k}{p}\right) = \frac{1}{2}(p-1)$
4) $\frac{k}{p} = \frac{1}{4}(p-1)(k-1) - 3\left[\frac{k}{p}\right] - \left[\frac{2k}{p}\right] - 3\left[\frac{3k}{p}\right] -$
$= \frac{1}{4}(p-1)(k-1) - 2\left\{\left[\frac{k}{p}\right] + \left[\frac{3k}{p}\right] + \left[\frac{5k}{p}\right] \ldots \left[\frac{(p-3)k}{p}\right]\right\} - \left\{\left[\frac{k}{p}\right] + \left[\frac{2k}{p}\right] + \left[\frac{3k}{p}\right] \ldots + \left[\frac{\frac{1}{2}(p-1)k}{p}\right]\right\}$

$\left[\frac{p}{k}\right]\, 0$
$\left[\frac{2p}{k}\right] - \left[\frac{p}{k}\right]\, 1$
$\left[\frac{3p}{k}\right] - \left[\frac{2p}{k}\right] \cdot 2$

$[x] + [2x] + [3x] \ldots + [nx] = 0\left[\frac{1}{x}\right]$
$+ 1\left\{\left[\frac{2}{x}\right] - \left[\frac{1}{x}\right]\right\}$
$+ 2\left\{\left[\frac{3}{x}\right] - \left[\frac{2}{x}\right]\right\}$
$\vdots$
$+[h]\left\{ n - \left[\frac{h}{x}\right]\right\}$

$[nx] = h$

$\left.\begin{array}{l}[x] + [2x] + [3x] \ldots + [nx] \\ + \left[\frac{1}{x}\right] + \left[\frac{2}{x}\right] + \left[\frac{3}{x}\right] \ldots + \left[\frac{h}{x}\right]\end{array}\right\} = nh$

$0{,}31 \quad 0{,}62 \quad 0{,}93 \quad 1{,}24$
$\frac{1}{0{,}31}$
$1 + 3 = 4$

methods.what: Definition of the counting symbol (k/p) (Gauss's lemma count) and of the floor-type bracket [x]

methods.what: Expression of the count (k/p) as alternating sums of greatest-integer values
Reflection identity for the bracket function
Relation between counts for k and −k
Formula for (k/p) in terms of (p−1)(k−1)/4 and sums of brackets of odd and all multiples
Lattice-point reciprocity: sum of [ix] for i≤n plus sum of [j/x] for j≤h equals nh where h=[nx]
Abel-type summation rewriting sum of [ix] via differences of [j/x]
